text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Soldier opens fire in Hebron, six hurt. Palestinian Authority apparently won't make new demands despite shooting.
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman: The sooner we sign on Hebron, the better.
- Shekem sells food interests to Super-Sol for 250 million shekels.
- Bank Hapoalim cuts non-banking affairs. Bank Leumi sells Ihud Insurance to Binyan for 32 million shekels.
- Labour Minister Eli Yishai to cancel 14,000 foreign-worker permits.
- Tel Aviv Stock Exchange: Shares traded abroad must be cross-listed.
GLOBES
- Globes ranking: Leaders in operating provident funds in 1996: International Bank and Mercantile-Discount Bank.
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor: Lower the interest rate.
HAARETZ
- Attacker: I wanted to halt the agreement. Army checking whether he was fit to receive a weapon. "I'm not crazy. I wanted to kill Arabs," he tells investigators.
- Additional delay in negotiations on Hebron agreement following new Palestinian demands for security arrangements.
- Deputy Prime Minister Rafael Eitan sent letter before the attack telling Netanyahu: "The negotiators don't understand the Arabs."
MAARIV
- Insanity in the heart of Hebron. Netanyahu: "The criminal act won't prevent the agreement".
- Commentary: Netanyahu neutralised the explosion.
- Hamas leaflet threatens: The revenge will be swift.
- Meridor: There will be nothing more to cut; we'll be forced to increase tax revenues.
- 596 killed, 3,414 injured in traffic accidents nationwide in 1996.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Insanity in Hebron.
- Meridor: "We did it" after budget passes.
